title: Gold and iron alike
hook: the one to whom praise and blame, gold and iron are the same (Salok M9, ang 1427)

segments.voice: Yesterday, moorat: untouched by the waves inside, clear enough to show God's image. Today, the voices outside.

A performance review lands in your inbox. Four paragraphs of praise, and one line that says you could communicate more clearly. Guess which line gets replayed on the drive home. The praise fades by dinner; the criticism rides along like a stone in a shoe. Or the reverse: one big compliment and you float for days, and then you need another. Either way, someone else's voice is holding the steering wheel. Guru Tegh Bahadur's fourteenth salok describes a person who has taken the wheel back.
screen: `FOUR PARAGRAPHS OF PRAISE.` → `ONE LINE ON THE DRIVE HOME.` → `WHO HOLDS THE WHEEL?`

segments.voice: The salok begins ustat nindiaa naahi jih, kanchan loh samaan. In paraphrase: the one for whom there is no praise and no slander, to whom gold and iron are the same: says Nanak, listen, O mind, know that one to be liberated. Ustat is praise. Nindiaa is slander, blame, talking someone down. Kanchan is gold, and loh is iron, the everyday metal of pots and plows. Samaan is equal, alike. The salok doesn't say this person never gets praised or blamed. Praise and blame just have no hook to catch on. Then it sets two metals side by side. Gold glitters; it's what we'd like to be called. Iron is ordinary. The salok asks for the same calm when someone calls you iron as when someone calls you gold. Back on day five hundred eighty-two, in a Sorath hymn, gold and dust were seen alike. Here it's gold and iron. The ninth Guru keeps returning to this picture, as if it's worth hearing more than once. And notice the last word: mukat, liberated. Sikh teaching speaks of jeevan mukat, someone free while still alive. Freedom here isn't a place you go after death. It's a person at a desk, reading a review, who can take the praise and the one line of criticism with the same steady face, learn from both, and stay themselves. Not to stop hearing what people say, but to stop being steered by it.
screen: `USTAT, NINDIAA: PRAISE AND BLAME.` · `KANCHAN, LOH: GOLD AND IRON.` · `SAMAAN: THE SAME.` · `MUKAT: FREE WHILE ALIVE.` · then, large: `GOLD AND IRON ALIKE.`

segments.voice: Bring back the last compliment you got and let its little lift settle; then a recent criticism, and let its sting settle too. Hold them side by side, like a gold coin and an iron nail in your two open hands, ask of each whether there's something true to learn, and then set both down. If you pray, you can rest in Waheguru between breaths.
Kanchan, gold. The fourteenth salok says the one for whom praise and blame, kanchan and loh, iron, are the same is mukat, free.
Your line: take the wheel back. Gold or iron, the same steady face. Day five hundred ninety-four, done.

howItsDone: Sikhs hear the fourteenth salok among Guru Tegh Bahadur's saloks at the close of a complete reading of the Guru Granth Sahib, and speak of jeevan mukat, being free while alive, as its ideal.

fork.setup: your review has four paragraphs of praise and one line of criticism. what does the fourteenth salok describe?
options: hold onto the praise and ignore the rest.
take both the same, gold and iron alike.

original.note: Gurmukhi: kanchan, gold. The salok sets it beside loh, iron, and calls them the same.

trapdoor: what you thought: gold and iron alike means not caring about money.
what it means: it means praise and blame, the shiny and the ordinary, stop steering you.
what a scholar hears: the salok sets precious gold beside plain iron and ties the pair to mukat, naming freedom as something visible in a living person's steadiness.
guess: iron, the metal of pots and plows
praise that lifts you for days

chat.says: How do I stop one bad comment from ruining my whole week?
options: The salok says hold praise and blame alike, like gold and iron: learn from both, stay yourself.
The salok says ignore every comment people make, good or bad, and never listen.
The salok says collect more praise, so the bad comments get outweighed by good ones.
chat.meaning: Ustat nindiaa naahi jih, kanchan loh samaan: praise and blame, gold and iron, alike. That one is mukat, free while alive.
